ADR.description: A structured framework for documenting architectural decisions, capturing context, alternatives considered, and rationale behind chosen approaches.

AI.description: Technology and methodologies for creating intelligent machines and automated systems that can perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence.

AI Agents.description: Autonomous software entities that can perceive their environment, make decisions, and take actions to achieve specific goals through API interactions.

API.description: Set of protocols, routines, and tools for building software applications, defining how software components should interact.

API Design.description: The practice of creating well-structured, intuitive, and maintainable interfaces for software applications and services.

Best Practices.description: Practical habits and conventions that keep code maintainable, consistent and efficient across a team and over the lifetime of a project.

Blogging.description: The practice of writing and publishing technical content to share knowledge, insights, and experiences with the developer community.

C#.description: Microsoft's statically typed, object-oriented programming language for .NET, covering language features, idioms and compiler behavior.

Design Patterns.description: Reusable solutions to commonly occurring problems in software design and architecture.

Events.description: Write-ups of conferences, meetups and community events, including talks given as a speaker and the slides that go with them.

Hosting.description: Choices and trade-offs in where and how websites and applications run, from servers and static hosting to deployment pipelines and costs.

.NET.description: Microsoft's open-source developer platform and runtime for building web, cloud, desktop and mobile applications, including ASP.NET Core.

Security.description: Techniques and configuration for protecting web applications and their users, such as security headers, policies and threat mitigation.

Software Architecture.description: The fundamental organization of a software system, including its components, relationships, and design principles.

Team Collaboration.description: Practices and methodologies for effective teamwork in software development, including communication, decision-making, and knowledge sharing.

Technical Writing.description: Specialized form of communication that conveys complex technical information clearly and effectively to specific audiences.

Umbraco.description: The open-source .NET content management system, covering implementation, editor experience, hosting and the Umbraco community.
